newsitem.title: USA: U.S. home mortgage rates up in week - Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: U.S. home mortgage rates up in week - Freddie Mac.

text.p: U.S. home mortgage rates rose this week as remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan revived fears of inflation, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.65 percent in the week ending Feb. 28, up from 7.56 last week, while 15-year mortgage rates increased to 7.15 percent from 7.06 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates also inched up to 5.49 percent from 5.45 percent last week, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 7.41 percent, the 15-year 6.87 percent and the adjustable loan 5.38 percent.

"Interest rates started rising when (Chairman) Alan Greenspan of the Federal Reserve advised the Senate Banking Committee that although the economy is in generally good shape, the financial markets should use caution," said Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist.
"Consequently, not only are interest rates up this week, but we expect they will rise even more by next week, perhaps to about 7.75 percent," Van Order added.
The central bank chairman on Wednesday gave his seminannual Humphrey Hawkins economic testimony to Congress.
On Friday the National Association of Realtors will issue U.S. January existing home sales data.
Lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. Charges on adjustable loans were also unchanged at 1.4 percent.
